Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The Australian players make their way out to the middle before spreading out and taking on their respective field positions. Abhishek Sharma and Shubman Gill are the two openers for India. Xavier Bartlett to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... The Run Chase ...

With both teams evenly matched, the outcome hinges on how well India handles the new ball threat from Xavier Bartlett and Sean Abbott. Can they rise to the occasion and clinch the win, or will Australia's bowlers prove too strong? We'll find out soon.

With India needing to chase 187, they'll need to be razor-sharp to overcome the Aussie challenge. With a talented batting lineup, the visitors can certainly pull off the win, but they'll need to be calculated and aggressive in their approach. The absence of Josh Hazlewood from the Australian attack will be a welcome relief for India.

The Indian bowlers shone, with Arshdeep Singh and Varun Chakravarthy taking crucial wickets. Arshdeep set the tone early, while Varun claimed two wickets in succession. Shivam Dube contributed with Tim David's significant wicket. Notably, Washington Sundar was left unused, likely due to the right-hand dominance in Australia's batting lineup, sparking questions about India's strategy, particularly regarding Kuldeep Yadav's exclusion.

Australia's formidable total of 186 was fueled by Tim David's explosive 74 and Marcus Stoinis' brilliant batting. Despite India's promising start, courtesy of Arshdeep Singh's early success with Travis Head, Australia's middle order seized control. David, promoted up the order, unleashed a furious 74 before falling to Shivam Dube, while Marcus Stoinis consistently threatened the Indian bowlers, scoring in the 60s.
A couple of runs to end the innings then! Arshdeep Singh goes much fuller and on off, Xavier Bartlett drills it down towards long off and comes back for the second run. Australia finish on 186/6!

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, wide of off, Tim David leans low and looks to cut this square but gets beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Jasprit Bumrah to Tim David, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and wide of off, Mitchell Marsh looks to flat bat this over cover but gets an inside edge that drops behind the stumps and rolls to fine leg for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Jasprit Bumrah to Mitchell Marsh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length on the pads, Mitchell Marsh tucks this to short mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Jasprit Bumrah to Mitchell Marsh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bumper, around off, going away from the batter. Tim David mistimes the pull around the surface towards leg for no run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Arshdeep Singh to Tim David, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length around the pads, Tim David flicks this towards Shivam Dube at square leg. Dube misfields it a bit but does well to make up and restrict this to a dot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Arshdeep Singh to Tim David, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Tim is promoted up in the order and he finds his striking range straight upfront. Pitched up around off, Tim David strides to the pitch of it and drives this through the gap between mid off and extra cover for four runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Arshdeep Singh to Tim David, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Tim David walks out next to bat.

OUT! CAUGHT! Double delight for Singh as he picks up Josh Inglis as well. On a length around the pads, Josh Inglis leans inside the line and picks it up with a flick, looking to take on the fielder at deep backward square leg. Josh hits this into the breeze and the ball fails to clear the fence and Josh Inglis is caught well inside by Axar Patel. Inglis walks back for a scratchy 1 off 7, and Australia are 14/2!
Commentary.Howout: c Axar Patel b Arshdeep Singh
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Arshdeep Singh to Josh Inglis, OUT! c Axar Patel b Arshdeep Singh.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length around the pads again, Marsh tucks this through square leg for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Arshdeep Singh to Mitchell Marsh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: LEG BYE! On a length, down the leg, Josh Inglis misses out on the flick and gets it clipped off the pads to short fine for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Arshdeep Singh to Josh Inglis, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Slower one, on a good length around off, Mitchell Marsh plays this early but does well to punt this short of cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Jasprit Bumrah to Mitchell Marsh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and wide outside off, Josh Inglis thumps this into the surface and towards Axar Patel at point. Patel does well to time his jump and field this but the batters take one in the process.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Jasprit Bumrah to Josh Inglis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length around off, Josh Inglis guides this to backward point..
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Jasprit Bumrah to Josh Inglis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Courageous of Josh Inglis to attempt this stroke off Bumrah. Good length, angling sharply into the batter. Josh Inglis looks to play the reverse ramp but gets beaten and is hit on his thigh pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Jasprit Bumrah to Josh Inglis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length around off, Mitchell Marsh pushes this to mid on and rotates strike.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Jasprit Bumrah to Mitchell Marsh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Bumrah is greeted with a boundary first up from Mitchell Marsh. On a length, angling into the batter, Mitchell Marsh leans inside the line of it and flicks this over square leg for a boundary to open his account.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Jasprit Bumrah to Mitchell Marsh, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Jasprit Bumrah will operate from the other end.

Good length, shaping away from the right-hander, Josh Inglis pushes this to point for another dot. An excellent start to the contest for India from Arshdeep Singh as he picks up Head and gives away just 6 off it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Arshdeep Singh to Josh Inglis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length around off, Josh Inglis dabs this to backward point for a dot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Arshdeep Singh to Josh Inglis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Josh Inglis walks out at 3.

OUT! CAUGHT! Arshdeep Singh needed just 4 deliveries to show his worth as he picks up the dangerous Travis Head. Good length, shaping away from the left-hander. Travis Head stays leg side to it and throws his bat at it. Gets it ballooned off the bottom of his bat over the Indian skipper at extra cover. Suryakumar Yadav settles well underneath this and grabs hold of it.
Commentary.Howout: c Suryakumar Yadav b Arshdeep Singh
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Arshdeep Singh to Travis Head, OUT! c Suryakumar Yadav b Arshdeep Singh.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Errs in line a little bit and Head was all over it. Good length, going down the leg, Travis Head hops up on his toes and flicks this through the short fine leg region for a boundary. The fielder was standing really square and Head makes use of this pocket towards fine leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Arshdeep Singh to Travis Head, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Singh finds the radar right. Good length, on top of off, Travis Head defends this off his back foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Arshdeep Singh to Travis Head, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Head and Australia are underway with a couple. Arshdeep Singh shows his rusty side and bowls a short and wide delivery first up, Travis Head punches this through the gap between cover and extra cover for a couple.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Arshdeep Singh to Travis Head, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to kick off in Hobart. India's Arshdeep Singh is ready to bowl the first over of the contest to Australia's dynamic opening duo of Mitchell Marsh and Travis Head.

Australian skipper, Mitchell Marsh, described the wicket as a 'belter' and expressed his hopes for a strong start. Marsh confirmed that the only change to the team would be Sean Abbott replacing Josh Hazlewood.

Suryakumar Yadav, the skipper of India, cannot stop smiling after finally winning the toss. He says that the wicket looks good, and with the temperature dropping, he expects it to come better on the bat in the second innings. Mentions that the atmosphere in the squad is very good and they want to take one game at a time. Says that every match is important for them and they want to focus on what's in front of them. Informs that they have made three changes. Jitesh Sharma, Arshdeep Singh, and Washington Sundar replaces Sanju Samson, Harshit Rana, and Kuldeep Yadav.

Australia (Playing XI) - Mitchell Marsh (C), Travis Head, Josh Inglis (WK), Tim David, Mitchell Owen, Marcus Stoinis, Matthew Short, Xavier Bartlett, Nathan Ellis, Matthew Kuhnemann, Sean Abbott (replaces Josh Hazlewood).

India (Playing XI) - Shubman Gill, Abhishek Sharma, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Tilak Varma, Axar Patel, Shivam Dube, Jitesh Sharma (WK) (replaces Sanju Samson), Washington Sundar (replaces Kuldeep Yadav), Varun Chakaravarthy, Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh (replaces Harshit Rana).
TOSS - Finally, Suryakumar Yadav has won a coin flip for India and he has elected to BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Aaron Finch is pitchside. He says that it is a bit windy but the sun is out too. Adds that the pitch is hard and it will be a good batting track. Mentions that the pacers will have some good carry and bounce but spinners will have a limited role. Ends by saying that the boundaries are short on one side and he expects a lot of runs.

Today's excitement is not limited to the men in blue, as the women in blue are gearing up to face South Africa Women in the highly anticipated Women's ODI World Cup final in Navi Mumbai. With both teams having never won the title, the stakes are high, and a new champion will be crowned. Meanwhile, India and Australia's men's teams will clash in a thrilling T20I match, where the bilateral series is tilted towards the Aussies at the moment. Huge expectations surround both matches, promising an electrifying day of cricket.

The stakes are high for India, as they cannot afford to lose this game if they want to stay in contention for the series. Abhishek Sharma's scintillating 68 in the previous match wasn't enough to prevent Australia's victory, but Suryakumar Yadav's side will look to regroup and return to winning ways. The match promises to be electrifying, with Australia looking to stretch their lead and India looking to bounce back and get level in series.

The Australian team might see some changes in the playing XI, with Sean Abbott likely to replace the departing Josh Hazlewood. Meanwhile, Glenn Maxwell's return to the squad would have boosted the team's morale, which was already on a high. Maxwell is expected to be fit to play in Hobart. India, on the other hand, will be looking to bounce back after a disappointing loss and might consider bringing Arshdeep Singh back into the XI, potentially at the expense of Kuldeep Yadav or Harshit Rana, and even replacing Sanju Samson with Jitesh Sharma.

Hello and welcome to everyone tuning in. The stage is set for an exciting encounter between India and Australia in the third T20I of the five-match series at the Bellerive Oval in Hobart. Australia currently leads the series 1-0 after securing a comprehensive win in the second T20I at the MCG. In that match, Australia's bowlers, led by Josh Hazlewood's match-winning spell, restricted India to just 125 runs, and the Aussies chased down the target with ease, thanks to a blistering start from Mitchell Marsh and Travis Head.
... MATCHDAY ...

The action shifts to the Bellerive Oval in Hobart for the third T20I between Australia and India. The series opener was washed out, but we managed to get a full game in Melbourne, where Australia produced a comprehensive win. They will be eyeing a 2-0 lead and an unassailable advantage in the five-match series. That victory at the MCG was built on the back of a disciplined bowling display, led by the ever-reliable Josh Hazlewood. His trademark precision set the tone before Mitchell Marsh broke the back of the 126-run chase inside the Powerplay, turning the rest into a mere formality. With Hazlewood now departing for Ashes preparations, Australia will look to maintain that same intensity in his absence. In his absence, Xavier Bartlett and Nathan Ellis will spearhead the pace department, with Sean Abbott likely to come in as Hazlewood’s replacement. However, a debut for Under-19 World Cup-winning speedster Mahli Beardman cannot be ruled out. The home side will receive a boost in both departments, with Glenn Maxwell joining the squad from the third T20I. Mitchell Owen is expected to make way for Maxwell, who returns after sitting out the New Zealand series with a fractured wrist. As for India, it was a dismal batting display in Melbourne, with Abhishek Sharma standing tall as the lone warrior. The visitors struggled against the seam movement and extra bounce on offer, and if they are to bounce back in Hobart, they will need the likes of Shubman Gill, Tilak Varma, and captain Suryakumar Yadav to step up. On the bowling front, it remains to be seen whether India persist with their three-pronged spin attack or bring in an extra pacer should conditions demand, with Arshdeep Singh waiting in the wings. Axar Patel injured himself while attempting a dive during his run-out and subsequently did not bowl, leaving a question mark over his availability for the Hobart fixture. India will be playing their first game in Hobart since 2012. It will be all about adapting to the conditions quickly. With overcast skies expected during the night, the pacers could have a major role to play. Which side will read the conditions better and come out on top in Hobart? We shall find out together.
